moves.move_text_short: set up parameterized family of NLS on metric graph and isolate a regime (Morse index bounded, λ_n→∞), decoupling from existence
moves.why_not: This is problem setup / scope-narrowing by parameter regime, not a mapping to a different formal system or any of the listed structural moves; v5 has no 'regime isolation / scoping' op.

moves.move_text_short: adapt Morse index from Euclidean PDE to metric-graph setting by replacing test-function space with H^1(G) ∩ C_c(G)
moves.why: A foundational definition (Morse index) is broadened so it makes sense in a new categorical setting (metric graphs), unifying the Euclidean and graph cases — exactly Framework Generalization.

moves.move_text_short: Liouville-type rigidity ruling out finite-Morse-index solutions on a star graph (W≡0), via oscillation argument with disjointly supported test functions
moves.why_not: This is a rigidity/non-existence theorem proved by a tailored oscillation argument; it is neither a domain translation nor an extremal-case reduction nor any other v5 mechanism — it's a domain-specific lemma.

moves.move_text_short: develop maximum principle for metric graphs handling vertex condition; complement with strong maximum principle
moves.why: Partly a generalization of a classical PDE tool (max principle) into the graph setting (core_07), but it's also just a tool-development step; coverage is half — only the abstraction half of core_07.

moves.move_text_short: construct explicit cosh comparison function on bounded interval as reusable 'exponential majorant' lemma
moves.why_not: Building an explicit barrier/comparison function is a technical-construction move; v5 has no op for 'auxiliary-object construction', and it isn't a partition, generalization, or transport.

moves.move_text_short: ODE convexity argument: local max of |u| is either ≥ fixed height or u vanishes on incident edges — quantitative threshold driving blow-up alternative
moves.why_not: Domain-specific ODE convexity dichotomy producing a quantitative lemma; not a domain translation, decomposition, or extremal-case reduction in the v5 sense.

moves.move_text_short: split blow-up analysis into two cases by comparing |u_n(x_n)|^{(p−2)/2} dist(x_n,V) against +∞: maxima away from vertex vs accumulating
moves.why: A case split into two geometrically distinct regimes resembles partial canonical decomposition (partition into well-understood pieces) — half of core_03's mechanism without explicit gluing.

moves.move_text_short: rescale u_n at blow-up point with ε_n to normalize maximum, use Ascoli-Arzelà + diagonal extraction + weak-* compactness to pass to a limit profile NLS
moves.why: Rescaling-and-pass-to-limit transports the problem from finite-λ NLS on G to a limit NLS on R or G_k, partially instantiating Problem Domain Translation (rescaling bridge) but is also a compactness argument.

moves.move_text_short: show limit profile inherits positive lower bound on frequency and Morse index 1≤·≤lim m(u_n), transferring spectral info from prelimit to limit
moves.why_not: This is a property-inheritance step under a limit; not a v5 op (not iterative refinement, not decomposition, not bootstrapping a weak property to strong).

moves.move_text_short: iterative selection procedure: produce maximal sequence of well-separated blow-up points by repeatedly choosing maxima far from previous points
moves.why: Greedy iterative procedure that monotonically extracts well-separated blow-up points until a termination/saturation condition is reached — direct instance of Iterative Refinement Loop's mechanism.

moves.move_text_short: cap number of blow-up points by m* via localized test functions giving linearly independent negative directions, contradicting Morse-index bound
moves.why: Uses an extremality/maximality argument (more than m* points would violate the Morse-index extremal constraint) — captures half of Extremal Case Analysis's rigidity mechanism.

moves.move_text_short: combine max principle with piecewise graph-wide barrier (cosh segments + exponentials, glued at vertices) to upgrade local exponential decay to global
moves.why: Local exponential decay near each blow-up point is glued (transmission through vertices) into a global decay estimate via consistency at vertices — textbook Local-to-Global Inference.

moves.move_text_short: subdivide edges by inserting auxiliary degree-2 vertices where global distance function changes expression, so dn becomes affine on each refined edge
moves.why_not: Edge-subdivision is a technical refinement of the underlying combinatorial domain to make a function affine; not a generalization, decomposition into well-understood components-with-glue, or any other v5 op.

moves.move_text_short: translate global exponential decay into integral asymptotic (1.5): λ_n^{(1/2−q/(p−2))}∫|u_n|^q → positive limit determined by limit profiles
moves.why_not: Quantitative consequence: a pointwise decay bound is integrated to derive an asymptotic; this is a corollary computation, not a structural move in v5.

moves.move_text_short: extract uniform-in-n bound on λ_n in L^2-prescribed regime when p≠6 — input for compactness in normalized-solution theory
moves.why_not: Direct corollary of the previous asymptotic; positions the result as input to other theory but does not perform a v5 structural operation.

moves.move_text_short: four-star example showing m of selected blow-up points need not match local maxima count; discrepancy hidden in limit profile
moves.why_not: An illustrative counterexample to clarify the theorem statement; v5 has no 'illustrative example / sharpness witness' op.

moves.move_text_short: pivot from blow-up analysis to a priori bounds; relate four numerical invariants (nodal zones, Morse index, L^∞, L^2) and how each inequality can fail
moves.why_not: This is a thematic pivot and statement of relations among invariants — a roadmap step, not an instantiation of a v5 structural mechanism.

moves.move_text_short: adapt Bahri–Lions classical lower bound of Morse index by active nodal zones to graphs; explicit triple-bridge example shows strict inequality
moves.why: Imports a classical Bahri–Lions theorem from Euclidean PDE as a black-box-like toolkit, verifying preconditions in the new graph setting — External Framework Importation.

moves.move_text_short: lower bounds on λ for given Morse index: separate compact case (eigenvalue of linearized operator) from half-line case (λ ≥ −inf lim W)
moves.why: Splits the geometric setting into two well-understood pieces (compact vs half-line) and proves the bound on each — partial decomposition without an explicit global gluing step.

moves.move_text_short: convert Hartman ODE result on superlinear equations into per-edge L^∞ bound on graphs by exploiting one-dimensional nature of each edge
moves.why: A classical Hartman ODE theorem is imported as an external black-box module, with edge-wise preconditions verified to apply it in the graph setting.

moves.move_text_short: establish converse: L^∞ bound forces Morse-index bound on compact graphs (sharp), failing on noncompact (tadpole, Z-periodic counterexamples)
moves.why_not: A converse direction with sharpness counterexamples; not duality framing (no dual problem solved jointly) and not a v5 structural mechanism.

moves.move_text_short: matching upper/lower L^2 bounds in λ for large λ from (1.5); refine small-λ behavior across three geometric settings (compact / localized / half-line)
moves.why: Enumerates three canonical geometric settings and verifies the picture in each — partially Systematic Cataloging (canonical-types enumeration) but without a coverage-completeness claim.

moves.move_text_short: demonstrate sharpness of small-λ exponent λ^{−1/4} via tadpole-graph construction: implicit-function/continuity at periodic backbone gives U_λ blowing up at that rate
moves.why_not: Sharpness witness via an explicit construction; v5 has no op for 'sharpness counterexample construction' (probabilistic_existence requires randomness).

moves.move_text_short: appendix records conserved energy and existence of sign-changing periodic solutions of underlying NLS ODE
moves.why_not: Bookkeeping of one-dimensional ODE prerequisites in an appendix; not a structural move — it just records facts the main constructions rely on.
